A bitters-soaked sugar cube and a splash of cognac in each flute, topped with brut champagne and a twist of lemon. Put a sugar cube in each of 4 flutes and shake 2 dashes of aromatic bitters onto each. Add 15ml cognac to each glass. Top slowly with 120ml chilled brut champagne, letting the sugar fizz. Twist a strip of lemon peel over each glass and drop it in.

s.note: Crisp pork and chive dumplings with black vinegar and chilli oil.
s.how: Heat 1 tbsp neutral oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add 12 frozen pork and chive dumplings and pan-fry for 3 minutes until their bottoms crisp. Add 80ml water and immediately cover. Steam for 7 to 9 minutes, or the packet time, until cooked through; remove the lid and let the water evaporate. Mix 2 tbsp black vinegar, 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp chilli oil for dipping.

s.note: Iced prawns on shredded iceberg with sharp cocktail sauce.
s.how: Poach 500g green prawns in simmering salted water for 2 minutes, plunge into iced water, peel and chill. Mix 125ml tomato sauce with 2 tsp horseradish, the juice of half a lemon and a dash of Worcestershire. Fill 4 glasses with shredded iceberg, hang the prawns over the rims and spoon the sauce in the middle.

m.note: Seared rib eye, creamy brandy peppercorn sauce and crisp frites.
m.how: Cut 800g potatoes into thin frites, rinse and dry thoroughly. Fry in neutral oil at 140°C for 5 minutes, drain and cool, then fry at 185°C for 3 minutes until crisp. Season with salt. Pat dry four 200g rib eye steaks and season. Heat 1 tbsp neutral oil in a heavy pan, sear the steaks for about 3 minutes each side to your preferred doneness, then rest 8 minutes. For sauce, add 1 tsp cracked black peppercorns to the pan, then carefully add 40ml brandy away from the flame. Simmer 1 minute, add 150ml beef stock and reduce for 5 minutes. Add 100ml thickened cream and simmer 3 minutes. Serve steaks with sauce and frites.

w.note: Cream cheese and sour cream filling on a buttery biscuit base.
w.how: Line a 16cm springform tin and wrap the outside tightly in two layers of foil. Crush 120g digestive biscuits, mix with 50g melted butter and press into the base. Beat 450g cream cheese with 100g caster sugar until smooth, then beat in 80g sour cream, 2 eggs and zest of 1 lemon. Pour into the tin. Put the tin in a roasting pan and add hot water halfway up its sides. Bake at 150°C conventional for 70 minutes until the edges are set and the centre gently wobbles. Turn off the oven, leave the door ajar and cool inside for 1 hour. Refrigerate overnight. Cut into four generous slices.
